headline: Market Snapshot: November 10, 2026
summary: US equity futures mixed ahead of October CPI report. Monday's close: S&P 500 +2.35% to 7,549.94, Nasdaq +2.74% to 25,253.14. Oil near $91.83 (Brent), BTC near $74,228.
key_facts: Dow futures +0.39%, S&P futures +0.17%, Nasdaq 100 futures -0.01% pre-market

headline: S&P 500 futures rise as traders brace for crucial consumer inflation report
summary: US stock futures were mixed in early Tuesday trading with investors awaiting the October CPI inflation data. Dow E-minis rose 205 points (+0.39%), S&P 500 E-minis gained 12.5 points (+0.17%), and Nasdaq 100 E-minis dipped 3 points (-0.01%) as of 5 a.m. ET.

headline: Dow surges 1,100 points, Nasdaq climbs more than 2% as tech rebounds from last week's tumult
summary: US stocks staged a strong rebound on Monday as tech and AI shares recovered from last week's post-midterm selloff. The S&P 500 jumped 2.35% to 7,549.94 for its best day since April 8, the Nasdaq Composite gained 2.74%, and the Dow rose more than 1,100 points (+2.15%).
key_facts: S&P 500 +2.35% to 7,549.94, best single day since April 8

headline: Asia Markets: Nikkei Surges, ASX 200 Climbs After Wall Street's 2.35% Jump
summary: Asian equity markets rose sharply on Tuesday November 10 following Wall Street's strong Monday session. Tokyo's Nikkei 225 led gains across the region, with ASX 200 also climbing. Technology and semiconductor stocks led the advance.
key_facts: Nikkei 225 led Asian gains on November 10
Tech and semiconductor stocks drove Asia rally

headline: European Shares Rally: DAX +1.73%, FTSE 100 +1.02% on Tuesday
summary: European equities rallied on Tuesday following the Wall Street rebound and falling oil prices. Germany's DAX closed 1.73% higher and the UK's FTSE 100 gained 1.02%, supported by easing geopolitical concerns over Iran and lower energy costs.

headline: October CPI due Tuesday: consensus +0.3% monthly, +4.0% year-over-year
summary: The October 2026 Consumer Price Index report is due Tuesday morning. The Dow Jones consensus calls for a 0.3% monthly headline rise and a 0.2% core increase, with annual headline CPI projected at around 4.0% year-over-year. A stronger print could cement a Fed rate hike in December.
key_facts: October CPI consensus: +0.3% MoM headline, +0.2% MoM core
BofA: beat would lock in 25bp Fed hike at December meeting
MUFG flags upside risk from airline fares, lodging, services

headline: Fed effective rate 3.88%; target raised to 3.75-4.00% in September, December hike expected
summary: The Fed effective funds rate stood at 3.88% as of early November 2026. The Fed raised its target range to 3.75–4.00% in September, its first hike since July 2023. Market participants and analysts anticipate a further 25bp increase at the December FOMC meeting if inflation remains elevated.
key_facts: December FOMC meeting December 8-9; hike expected if CPI hot

headline: Oil prices continue to fall on hopes of US-Iran peace deal talks; Brent near $91.83
summary: Crude oil prices extended their sharp decline on Tuesday as diplomatic hopes between the US and Iran continued to build. Brent crude fell to around $91.83 and WTI dropped to $86.33, with both benchmarks down roughly 20% in November. The Strait of Hormuz blockade remains in place, keeping a price floor in the low $90s.
key_facts: Brent crude ~$91.83, WTI ~$86.33 as of Nov 10
Brent at lowest level since late August
Strait of Hormuz blockade still in force

headline: Trump says US-Iran war 'effectively over' militarily after Qatar-mediated talks
summary: President Trump said the US-Iran war is 'effectively over' militarily following Qatar-mediated diplomatic talks, with fresh strikes described as 'quite unlikely'. Iran's proposals include lifting the naval blockade, repealing sanctions, and a regional ceasefire. Oil prices fell sharply as markets priced in reduced conflict risk.
key_facts: Iran proposes US lift naval Hormuz blockade, repeal sanctions
Republicans blamed war and high energy prices for midterm losses
Brent fell ~20% in November on diplomacy hopes

headline: Democrats sweep 2026 midterms, taking both House and Senate; Dow surges 3% then tech tanks
summary: Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in the November 3 midterm elections, projecting over 250 House seats and 54+ Senate seats. Markets initially rallied — Dow +3% (1,569 pts) on November 4 — but then reversed sharply on Thursday as investors worried Democratic control would slow AI data center construction, wiping ~$2.5 trillion in Nasdaq market cap.
key_facts: Democrats projected >250 House seats and 54+ Senate seats
Dow rose 1,569 pts (+3%) on Nov 4 post-election relief rally
Thursday selloff erased ~$2.5T in Nasdaq market cap
AI buildout concerns drove tech selloff
Trump accepted midterm results, reducing post-election uncertainty

headline: Nvidia stock falls 4.27% as board opens probe into CEO Jensen Huang's ties to alleged Chinese spy
summary: Nvidia shares fell 4.27% on Monday as the company's board launched an independent investigation after reports that CEO Jensen Huang had a relationship with a woman US intelligence considers a Chinese asset. Huang acknowledged the affair internally and said he remains committed to leading Nvidia. Analysts said leadership risk—not the affair itself—is the main investor concern, with Dan Ives noting Huang is 'not replaceable'.
key_facts: NVDA closed at $178.67 on November 9, down 4.27%
Nvidia board launched independent investigation into Huang
Huang acknowledged affair in internal memo
Company: 'Jensen is committed to leading Nvidia as CEO without interruption'

headline: Sanmina surges ~20% after Q4 FY2026 earnings beat: revenue $3.86B (+84% YoY), EPS $4.43 vs est $3.27
summary: Sanmina (SANM) reported fiscal Q4 2026 results that significantly beat expectations, with quarterly revenue of $3.86B (+84% YoY) versus the $3.48B estimate, and non-GAAP EPS of $4.43 vs the $3.27 consensus. Full-year revenue rose 79% to $14.5B. FY2027 revenue guidance of $17.5-$19.5B also exceeded forecasts, sending shares up roughly 19-20% pre-market.
key_facts: Q4 FY2026 revenue: $3.86B, +84% YoY, beat est $3.48B
FY2026 operating cash flow: $944M, free cash flow: $541M

headline: Take-Two Interactive Q2 FY2027: Net Bookings $1.60B (-18% YoY); GTA VI launch November 19
summary: Take-Two Interactive reported fiscal Q2 FY2027 results with Net Bookings of $1.60B, down 18% YoY from $1.96B, as recurrent consumer spending (81% of total) fell 9%. Revenue of ~$1.50B missed the ~$1.66-1.70B consensus. The company reaffirmed full-year FY2027 Net Bookings guidance of $8.0-8.2B, underpinned by Grand Theft Auto VI launching November 19.
key_facts: Recurrent consumer spending: 81% of bookings, -9% YoY

headline: CoreWeave Q3 2026 earnings due after close: 159% revenue growth expected vs $900M interest burden
summary: AI cloud provider CoreWeave (CRWV) is set to report Q3 2026 earnings after the market close on November 10. Analysts expect revenue of approximately $3.54B, representing ~159% growth, against management's guidance of $3.45-3.60B. The options market implies a ~21% post-earnings move. The company's $104.2B backlog and ~$900M quarterly interest expense are focal points.

headline: Vir Biotechnology stock jumps 22% after Phase 3 ECLIPSE 1 hepatitis delta trial meets all endpoints
summary: Vir Biotechnology reported that its Phase 3 ECLIPSE 1 trial of elebsiran and tobevibart combination therapy met all primary and key secondary endpoints in chronic hepatitis delta. The once-monthly injectable combination achieved 44% primary endpoint response (vs 0% delayed treatment) at Week 12, with 79% showing undetectable HDV RNA at Week 48. Vir plans FDA regulatory submission and shares rose 22% on the data.
key_facts: ECLIPSE 1 Phase 3 met primary and all key secondary endpoints
44% primary endpoint response (undetectable HDV RNA + ALT normalization) at Week 12 vs 0% control
79% with undetectable HDV RNA at Week 48
Data presented at AASLD Liver Meeting 2026, Denver, November 8

headline: Ionis Pharmaceuticals shares drop ~27% after Tryngolza 2026 sales guidance cut to ~$50M from $100-110M
summary: Ionis Pharmaceuticals (IONS) reported Q3 2026 revenue of $243M, well above the $183M estimate, but slashed its Tryngolza (olezarsen) full-year 2026 sales guidance to approximately $50M from $100-110M due to a slower-than-expected launch in severe hypertriglyceridemia. The stock fell roughly 25-27% to a 52-week low; Raymond James cut its price target to $54 from $79.
key_facts: Raymond James cut PT to $54 from $79, kept Outperform

headline: Marvell to buy Nvidia-backed Lumentum in $115B all-stock deal targeting AI optical interconnect
summary: Marvell Technology agreed to acquire Lumentum Holdings in an all-stock deal with an implied enterprise value of approximately $115 billion, the largest deal of 2026. Lumentum shareholders will receive 4.500 Marvell shares per share, a ~23.9% premium to the October 28 unaffected close. The deal targets AI optical interconnect infrastructure and is expected to close in H1 2028.
key_facts: Exchange ratio: 4.500 MRVL shares per LITE share
Expected close: H1 2028, pending regulatory and shareholder approvals

headline: Rocket Lab Q3 2026: record revenue $268M (+73% YoY), beats guidance; stock -6% pre-market
summary: Rocket Lab (RKLB) posted record Q3 2026 revenue of $268M, up 73% year-over-year and above its own guidance of $250-265M. The company secured over $515M in Neutron launch contracts during the quarter and reported positive GAAP operating cash flow of $7.2M. Backlog grew 52% since Q2 to approximately $3.6B. Despite the beat, shares fell ~6% pre-market on Monday after the report.
key_facts: Neutron launch contracts: >$515M secured in Q3

headline: Babcock & Wilcox Q3 2026: revenue $290.8M (up from $139.2M), EPS $0.61; stock +15% pre-market
summary: Babcock & Wilcox Enterprises (BW) reported Q3 2026 revenue of $290.8M, more than doubling from $139.2M in Q3 2025. Net income was $93.9M and diluted EPS was $0.61 vs $0.30 a year earlier. CEO Kenneth Young said results beat Street consensus. Full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance maintained at $80-105M. Shares were up ~15% in pre-market trading.
key_facts: Net income: $93.9M; EPS: $0.61 (vs $0.30 a year ago)

headline: Crypto market cautious ahead of CPI: Bitcoin ~$74,228, Ethereum ~$2,112; ETF outflows weigh
summary: Crypto markets were subdued on November 10 as investors awaited the US CPI report. Bitcoin traded at approximately $74,228, down 0.4% over 24 hours, while Ethereum was near $2,112, down 1.3%. Global crypto market cap stood at $2.59 trillion with Bitcoin dominance at 57.8%. Rising ETF outflows and deleveraging weighed on sentiment.
key_facts: Rising ETF outflows and liquidations cited

headline: Gold declines below $4,150 as rising Fed hike expectations outweigh US-Iran deal hopes
summary: Gold slipped back below $4,150/oz during Asian trading on Tuesday, reversing part of Monday's gains to a near three-week high. Rising Fed rate hike expectations ahead of October CPI acted as headwinds, while Iran diplomacy hopes provided modest support. 10-year Treasury yields held near 4.86%, anchoring the dollar.
key_facts: Gold below $4,150/oz in Asian session Nov 10
Monday: gold rallied to near 3-week high
Fed rate hike expectations for December capping gains

headline: Oppenheimer upgrades AMD to Outperform with $600 target; Citigroup initiates Uber at Buy $105
summary: Monday analyst calls: Oppenheimer upgraded Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) from Market Perform to Outperform with a $600 price target, citing improved AI chip sales trends. Citigroup initiated Uber Technologies at Buy with a $105 target. Citigroup also upgraded Rollins to Buy from Neutral, raising its target to $49 from $32. Stifel downgraded DraftKings to Hold from Buy, cutting the target to $21 from $32.
key_facts: Oppenheimer: AMD upgraded to Outperform, PT $600
Citigroup: Uber initiated at Buy, PT $105
Citigroup: Rollins upgraded to Buy, PT raised $32→$49
Stifel: DraftKings downgraded to Hold, PT cut $32→$21

headline: Stifel downgrades DraftKings to Hold, cuts price target to $21 from $32
summary: Stifel downgraded DraftKings (DKNG) to Hold from Buy, lowering its price target to $21 from $32, citing competitive pressures and a slower-than-expected growth ramp in legal US sports betting.
key_facts: Stifel: DKNG downgraded to Hold from Buy

headline: CKX Lands surges ~65% pre-market on $1B Brad Jacobs investment and special dividend
summary: CKX Lands (CKX) surged approximately 65% in pre-market trading on November 10 after announcing a $1 billion investment led by Brad Jacobs and a planned special dividend for existing shareholders.
key_facts: Special dividend planned for existing shareholders

headline: Bon Secours Mercy Health takes Surgery Partners private at $23.50/share; Bain Capital rolls equity
summary: Bon Secours Mercy Health agreed to take Surgery Partners (SGRY) private at $23.50 per share, with largest shareholder Bain Capital rolling over its equity stake. Law firms have opened shareholder investigations into the deal terms. The transaction is pending regulatory approvals.
key_facts: SGRY taken private at $23.50/share by Bon Secours Mercy Health
Bain Capital (largest shareholder) rolling over equity

headline: 10-year Treasury yield holds near 4.86% as markets brace for October CPI; 2-year at 4.55%
summary: The 10-year US Treasury yield steadied near 4.86% on November 9-10 as stronger-than-expected employment data reinforced December Fed rate hike expectations. The 2-year yield remained around 4.55%. The dollar weakened modestly on Monday, providing support to gold and silver.
key_facts: Dollar weakened Monday, reversed some Friday gains
December Fed hike expectation reinforced by strong jobs data

headline: Oil falls 5.8% with Brent at ~$92.57 on Iran peace talks; stocks lift on lower energy costs
summary: Oil fell 5.8% on Monday with Brent crude dropping to around $92.57 as Iran ceasefire diplomacy progressed, boosting global equities via lower energy costs. The fall contributed to Monday's broad market rally, particularly benefiting energy-intensive industries and consumer spending outlooks.
key_facts: Brent crude fell 5.8% to ~$92.57 on Monday
Iran diplomacy cited as key driver

headline: Analysts: Nvidia CEO unlikely ousted over Chinese spy affair, but governance questions ahead of Nov 17 earnings
summary: Wall Street analysts broadly said Jensen Huang is unlikely to be ousted as Nvidia CEO despite the board's investigation into his relationship with an alleged Chinese intelligence contact. Mizuho's Jordan Klein noted the probe will likely overshadow Nvidia's Q3 earnings report due November 17. Analysts including Dan Ives emphasized Huang's centrality to Nvidia's business and product vision.
key_facts: Analyst consensus: Huang unlikely to be ousted

headline: Kimberly-Clark completes acquisition of Kenvue on November 2, 2026
summary: Kimberly-Clark completed its acquisition of Kenvue (the former J&J consumer brands spinoff) on November 2, 2026, combining two major consumer staples businesses.
key_facts: Kimberly-Clark acquisition of Kenvue closed November 2, 2026

headline: Ferring acquires Gameto for up to $1.3825B in reproductive medicine deal
summary: Ferring Pharmaceuticals agreed to acquire fertility biotech Gameto for up to $1.3825B including milestone payments, expanding Ferring's reproductive medicine portfolio. The deal is part of a broader wave of biotech M&A activity in 2026 totaling $207.8B across 76 deals.
key_facts: Ferring acquires Gameto for up to $1.3825B including milestones
